To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

The Froissart bound on the p̄ p scattering amplitude at high energies is saturated, and that this saturation allows us to predict the p̄-air and p-air inelastic production cross sections with unprecedented accuracy, in both magnitude and energy dependence, at all energies of interest, including ultra-high energies.
the proton–air cross section at ultra-high energies is predicted to be σ p−air ≈ 1200 ± 200 μ b at √ s = 100000 Tev.

the predictions of σ p−air from accelerator data are in excellent agreement both with cosmic ray data and with predictions from a saturated version of the Froissart bound, and are in good agreement with predictions from the Gribov–Regge theory.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the physics of high energy scattering processes, and the extrapolations of accelerator data to the highest cosmic ray energies.

the development of a new approach to the analysis of accelerator data on high-energy proton-proton (pp) and antiproton-proton (p̄p) scattering, with a focus on the energy region √ s ≥ 100 GeV, which is relevant for the study of ultra-high energy cosmic rays.
the study of the proton–air cross section at the highest energies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cosmic-ray extensive air-shower data are in good agreement with the predictions of accelerator data and the Froissart bound.
there is a strong case that the Froissart bound is saturated, that there are no new resonances, and that the proton–air cross section is increasing with energy.

the cosmic ray extensive air showers data are in excellent agreement both in magnitude and energy dependence with the predictions of the saturated Froissart Bound parameterization of accelerator p̄p, pp and πp scattering amplitudes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cosmic ray data are in excellent agreement both with accelerator data and with the Froissart bound, and are consistent with the hypothesis of a universal proton-proton scattering amplitude.
the cosmic ray data, together with accelerator data, provide strong evidence for a saturated Froissard bound.
the Froissart bound and the Glauber theory are sufficient to describe cosmic ray extensive air showers, with no need for additional assumptions.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the Froissart bound is saturated at energies well below the highest energies measured at the LHC, and that the extrapolation of accelerator data to ultra-high energies can be done with great accuracy.

the proton–air cross section can be reliably extrapolated to energies far beyond the range of accelerator measurements, using only the accelerator data and a few analyticity and unitarity constraints.

the extrapolated cross sections are consistent with the predictions from the Froissart bound and with the extrapolated cosmic ray data, and that they are not consistent with a power-law energy dependence.
